reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text three times against saved copies of the Kannada Wikipedia article ಗೋವಿನ ಹಾಡು (song transcription and summary) and the Mysore University Vishwakosha entry.

Owner rule 2026-10-17 (never change plot or ending): the song's ending is kept, the tiger repents, leaps into the sky and gives up its life, with Shiva's release marked as what is said; told calmly, not drawn; contentNote states it plainly.

Restored after the owner rule: the three oaths, the river bath, the offer of her flesh, the farewell to the calf (ಸಾಯಬೇಕು, ತಬ್ಬಲಿ) and the tiger's threat (ಕೆಡವಿ ಸೀಳಿ). Small connecting details and ಗೊಲ್ಲ → ದನಗಾಹಿ are disclosed.
Age 10+: the villain dies as the story's consequence, in calm non-graphic words.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536; seams exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024; under 650 KB.
Calf removed from the two hillside panels (the calves stay in the enclosure); a calf-like animal in the distant herd replaced by adult cows; three panels composited from two edit passes.
No text, no modern objects, no blood.

Edit pass 3 removed the departing tiger from the last panel (the death is not drawn); a ~10px leftover tail curl on the ridge was covered with a 14x10 neighbouring-sky patch; reviewer zoomed and confirmed nothing tiger-like remains, seams exact.
Punyakoti keeps her white coat, two horns, red-yellow cord and bell; the tiger never touches her.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher, folklorist or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children or parents.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol in the new stylized 3D look for this collection, and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with seams measured in pixels.
Source fidelity was checked against the Wikipedia transcription and summaries, not a critical edition of the song.
